answer: Each agent identity can enter the market only by locking a scarce, nontransferable copper bond, then earning access to larger trades through repeated deliveries that counterparties verify and attest to. A lantern-style public ledger makes bond ownership and default history visible, while randomized checks compare delivered work with its claim, including a pigment sample chosen after submission. Spinning up aliases therefore requires separate capital and exposes each one to forfeiture; an attacker must fund many bonds and keep them credible, not merely mint names.
